palette.notes: Frames: dark blue-grey and brown cave rock, near-black voids; the light comes from the simulated matter: orange-yellow fire, sparks, red blood, pink crystal, blue water. Small blue-purple witch.

lighting: Darkness with emissive matter: fire, explosions and sparks light the area around them in a warm glow (clip 1, 5.7-8.3 s), the rest of the cave stays dim. Light moves with the effect.
silhouette: Tiny robed witch (minä, wiki) only a few pixels tall, readable by colour (blue-purple) against brown rock and by the wand flash. Enemies are small too; the world is the star.

motion.timing: No frame timings measured. Effects run per pixel each frame: sand falls and piles (clip 2), fire spreads, explosions throw particles that settle over ~2 s (clip 1).

texture: Every pixel is simulated material (falling-sand engine, wiki): sand, liquid, smoke, steam, blood. Walls are noisy speckled rock that breaks into loose pixels; burnt wood disappears into smoke (wiki).
camera: Side view that follows the witch; the explosion fills the screen and the camera holds while debris settles.

acting.enters: Witch walks in small from the edge of a big dark cave (clip 1).
acting.acts: Cause and effect is the acting: one wand shot sets off a chain of fire and explosion far bigger than the character.
acting.exits: Death screen is the punchline (clip 3, 'cause of death' card).
acting.depth: Character stays tiny; scale comes from the effect blooming large around her.

techniques: particle pixels that obey gravity: sand piles, smoke rises, steam rains back as water
emissive fire and sparks as the only bright light in a dark scene
tiny hero, huge consequence: small action, screen-filling effect
debris settles after the burst instead of vanishing
materials react: lava + water make rock and steam (wiki)
feel: dark cave + tiny witch + glowing pixel fire that spreads and settles = chaotic, cause-and-effect comedy
for_fred: Use one small Fred action that triggers a big pixel consequence (a splash that spreads, sparks that fall and pile up), then hold 1 s while the particles settle and Fred looks at it. The aftermath is the gag.
